--- title: "October 18–22, 2026" date: 2026-10-18 description: "Network median 2.24 in (range 1.18–3.62 in); peak IVT 412 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SSW" categories: [IVT ≥ 250, Snow, Final] execute: freeze: auto --- ## Summary Across 37 gauges the event total ranged from 1.18 to 3.62 in (median 2.24 in). The central 80% of the network-mean rain fell between Oct 21 05:00 MST and Oct 22 10:00 MST (29 h). Moisture transport over Flagstaff reached atmospheric-river strength: ERA5 IVT was at or above 250 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ for 42 h and peaked at 412 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SSW at Oct 21 11:00 MST. 98% of the network-mean rain fell while IVT was at or above 250. At the IVT peak, 500-hPa flow over Flagstaff was from the SSW at 28 m s⁻¹, and the 500-hPa trough axis along 35.25°N was at 126.2°W, 1,325 km west of Flagstaff (5,586 m, against 5,842 m over Flagstaff). A closed 500-hPa low (5,570 m) was centred 1,342 km to the W, at 34.0°N 126.2°W. The strongest 250-hPa wind within 1,000 km was 60 m s⁻¹, 731 km to the W. The 250-hPa wind over Flagstaff peaked at 43 m s⁻¹ (Oct 20 23:00 MST), 12 h before the IVT peak. ## Rain across the network ::: {#b93c6e22 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Event rain total at each city and county gauge (circle area proportional to total, labels in inches) over shaded relief (USGS 3DEP), 200-m elevation contours, streams (USGS NHD) and highways (Census TIGER). Step with the buttons, slider or ← → keys; space plays and pauses.* ## What the forecasters said The National Weather Service office in Flagstaff discussed the moisture source in its Area Forecast Discussions as the event unfolded. Excerpts, quoted verbatim (links to the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive): - **Oct 18, 2:03 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610180903)): "A southerly moisture surge is currently underway, somewhat enhanced by continued active tropical cyclone activity in the Eastern Pacific." - **Oct 19, 12:40 PM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610191940)): "On Wednesday and Thursday, the West Coast low shifts eastward toward northern Arizona allowing deep subtropical moisture to push into the area from the south. Some of this incoming moisture will be assocaited with what is currently Tropical Storm Trudy centered south of the Baja Peninsula." - **Oct 20, 2:47 PM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610202147)): "Some of this moisture is left over from post-tropical cyclone Trudy and is enhanced by the continued active tropical activity in the eastern Pacific." - **Oct 22, 3:00 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610221000)): "This system is pulling a rich subtropical moisture plume into the state, yielding record amounts of atmospheric moisture for this time of year." ## Climate context - **Airport precipitation:** 1.84 in over 5 local days, against a 1991–2020 normal of 0.24 in for those days (8× normal). - **Rank:** the 31st largest 5-day airport total in October among 129 years with data since 1898 (each year's largest 5-day total ending in October). - **Airport temperature:** highs averaged -2.0 °F and lows +10.2 °F relative to normal. - **Water year to date** (Oct 1, 2026 – Oct 22, 2026): airport 5.39 in (normal 1.08 in);
